paper.title: Lag: A Mean-Field Optimal Policy for Online Assignment with Reusable Resources

settings.name_in_paper: Online assignment with reusable resources as a contextual restless multi-armed bandit (CRMAB), discrete-time M/G/R/R loss system
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Planning/stochastic control of a restless (Markovian) bandit with fully known parameters (scores, arrival rates, service distributions); no learning; objective is long-run average reward rather than regret.
unmapped: Score matrix s_vr known; servers become busy for random bounded durations D_v <= d after assignment (reusable resources)
Exactly k free servers must be assigned per arrival (work-conserving); tasks dropped when fewer than k free
Objective is long-run average reward compared against an LP benchmark, in an (m,n) mean-field scaling
settings.definition_quote: We consider a pool of $R$ servers and a stream of tasks arriving in discrete time ... At a type-$v$ arrival, if at least $k$ servers are free the policy assigns a set $\mathcal{A}_t$ of exactly $k$ of them, yielding reward $\sum_{r \in \mathcal{A}_t} s_{v_t r}$; if fewer than $k$ are free the task is dropped

symbols.OPT_B: optimal value of the occupancy-measure LP OCC-LP(B) at blocking probability B

source.label: prop:lp_upper_bound
source.quote: For any work-conserving policy $\pi$, with $B$ the blocking probability of Lemma~\ref{lem:blocking}, \[ \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{A}_t} s_{v_t r} \leq \mathrm{OPT}(\text{OCC-LP}(B)). \]

results.notes: Upper bound on achievable long-run average reward (impossibility for any work-conserving policy); not a regret bound.

bound.regime: as m,n -> infinity in the (m,n)-scaled system

conditions: global attractor property of fluid map G (Assumption 4.2)

source.label: thm:asymptotic_optimality
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{assum:underload} and \ref{assum:gap}, in the $(m,n)$-scaled loss system, \[ \frac{\Reward_{m,n}(\Lag)}{mn} \longrightarrow \mathrm{OPT}(\text{OCC-LP}(0)) \qquad \text{as } m,n \to \infty, \] and limsup ... for every work-conserving policy. Hence \Lag\ is asymptotically optimal.

results.notes: Achievability half: normalized long-run average reward converges to LP value.

source.label: thm:asymptotic_optimality
source.quote: and $\displaystyle\limsup_{m,n\to\infty}\frac{\Reward_{m,n}(\pi)}{mn} \;\le\; \mathrm{OPT}(\text{\upshape OCC-LP}(0))$ for every work-conserving policy $\pi$.

results.notes: Converse half of Theorem 4.1: bound on reward of any work-conserving policy.

symbols.n_copies: per-dispatcher copies per server type (scaling n)
symbols.m_arr: number of arrivals per step (scaling m)

source.label: lem:mn_reward
source.quote: For every $m,n$ and every initial state $x(0)\in\mathcal{X}^{m,n}$, there exists a stationary distribution $\mu^{m,n}$ ... such that \left|\frac{\Reward_{m,n}(\Lag)}{mn} - \sum_{v,r} s_{vr}\int u_{vr}^{\Lag}(x)\,d\mu^{m,n}(x)\right| \le s_{\max}\left(\frac{4R}{\sqrt{n}}+\frac{R}{n}+k\,p_n +2k\,e^{-\gamma^2 m/(2k^2 d)}\right)

results.notes: Bound on gap between finite-system normalized reward of LAG and fluid reward under a stationary distribution; technical step toward Theorem 4.1.
